head: b7e9c181309d074c24213cb8ebe0947f71cb358d
summary: SL-095 shipped a workaround for the wcifs.sys leak (microsoft/Windows-Containers#646). C: scans now skip %ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers and show it as a 'size not counted' row. A picked root inside the store is refused. One 'wcifs-layer-store' checkbox in a new Settings window lifts both, per Q-186. It also added report fields, four fitness rules and a person-run PoolWatch harness. Spike #87 showed that a listing-only walk with the store excluded still grows paged pool by 375 MiB and nonpaged by 138 MiB (NtfF/FMfn/File). So the app change cannot meet DONE (c), and that criterion, along with the cause of the reported ~30 GB, moved to SC-128 after eight design laps.

payload.reason: SL-095 shipped the app-side workaround (DONE a/b) and left DONE (c) and the cause of the tens-of-GB growth unreached.
payload.summary: SL-095 shipped a workaround for the wcifs.sys leak (microsoft/Windows-Containers#646). C: scans now skip %ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers and show it as a 'size not counted' row. A picked root inside the store is refused. One 'wcifs-layer-store' checkbox in a new Settings window lifts both, per Q-186. It also added report fields, four fitness rules and a person-run PoolWatch harness. Spike #87 showed that a listing-only walk with the store excluded still grows paged pool by 375 MiB and nonpaged by 138 MiB (NtfF/FMfn/File). So the app change cannot meet DONE (c), and that criterion, along with the cause of the reported ~30 GB, moved to SC-128 after eight design laps.

learned.lesson: A slice whose done-when needs a person-run Restart and repeated whole-C: scans cannot close on loop evidence. Split it at open into the code fix and the measurement, or fix the narrowing decision up front. Do not open it as one medium bug fix.
learned.evidence: DONE (c), '5 full + 5 cancelled C: scans after a true Restart', was never reached. It moved to SC-128 only at design attempt 10, after 6 spikes, 8 designs, 8 critiques and 11 builds. Four of the six spike laps ended 'built anyway' because every decisive check needed a Restart.

learned.lesson: Do not build the verdict or judge half of a measurement harness before the fork it routes has been decided. Log raw nets and a completeness check first, and add judgement only once one real session's logs exist.
learned.evidence: The PoolWatch -Report judge (settle gate, per-pool drift VOID, tolerance row, A/B/C routing, pressure step, unfixed afd021d arms, WCIFS-UNATTRIBUTED) drew about seven code-review send-backs: R2-N1, R3-1, R4-1, R4-2, R2-R3-3, R3-2 and M1. Spike #87 then decided outcome C, and design 10 deleted the judge and handed it to SC-128. Build attempts 3-5 and 7-9 changed almost no src.

learned.lesson: When a slice re-enters design after builds, re-measure what exists and whether earlier build commits are reachable from the slice branch. Do not reuse the build-check taken at slice open.
learned.evidence: Design attempt 10 stated 'acf169eb's code is not on slice/SL-095, because the design's build check measured no source diff at afd021d. So everything is built new', and listed 'acf169eb being reachable' as what would change the decision. The only 'what exists' measurement was build-check #1, taken before builds #2-#6 had reviewed scanner code. The record does not show the reachability being checked.

learned.lesson: When a design hands a question to a person and the critique resolves it the other way, the build lands on the unanswered branch. Reversing it later touches code, user-facing text, tests and the architecture text together. Keep the branch decision in one place, or hold the user-facing wording until it is answered.
learned.evidence: Critique F1 made the picked-root refusal unconditional against the design's own off-lifts-both position. Q-186 then answered off-lifts-both. Validate #2/#3 failed criterion 7, and builds #7-#9 plus code-review #10-#11 reworked ContainerLayerStore.Resolve:95, KnownWorkarounds.IfTurnedOff, MainWindow.xaml.cs:503, X-005, X-006 and AA-015.

learned.lesson: The wcifs leak does not explain the report's magnitude, and the shipped workaround should not be read as having fixed 'out of memory after scanning C:'. The unattributed tags FMfn, File, NtfF and Toke dominate. Spike #87 measured about 800 B per directory open (537 MB over 669,824 listings), with the store excluded and no WC* rise. The SC-128 session must be sized assuming a cold full exe scan costs several GiB, and that the cause of the tens-of-GB growth is still unknown.
learned.evidence: Build-check: the wcifs group is about 290 MB of 8.3 GB. Spike #87: +375 MiB paged and +138 MiB nonpaged by the guard stop at 3.31M entries. Design arithmetic: a cold exe-full is predicted at 3-4.4 GiB, against the 6 GiB per-arm guard. Validate #6 reports that the tens-of-GB growth was not reached.

learned.lesson: The 'wcifs leaks only on first touch, capped near 0.33 GB per boot' claim is contested and must not be reused as a premise. The investigation measured 0 on a repeat walk. Validate #2 measured +5 WCsc/WCfc/WCri/FMwi and +5 System 0x120089 handles on each of 4 repeat walks of Files\Windows\Globalization. It named the app's SizeProbe opens of non-Offline reparse+sparse ICU files as the probable cause, but did not confirm it.
learned.evidence: Validate #2 marks: handles 3638->3643->3648, then 3648->3653->3658. The user-facing texts at KnownWorkarounds.cs:29, :38 and :46 had said 'read for the first time'. Critique M2 argued 'cannot build up scan after scan' from the first-touch cap. Both were corrected in build #7/#9.

learned.lesson: The layer store is matched by path spelling, and only GetFinalPathNameByHandleW is spelling-independent. Spellings an unelevated user can open still got past it. Any new root-spelling case must be checked through the published exe on the real store. Planted %TEMP% stores did not expose the loopback-share gap.
learned.evidence: Validate #2: \\localhost\C$\ProgramData\...\Layers\<id>\Files\Windows\Media was not refused. Outcome Completed, 95 files and 14 folders read from inside the store. It was fixed by mapping the \\<local>\X$ forms to X:\ in ContainerLayerStore. Still documented as unmatched: a net use drive mapped to \\localhost\C$, a hosts/DNS alias, an admin-created share over ProgramData, and other WCI stores.

learned.lesson: On this PC the engine's 0.5 GB per-run kernel-pool guard reads a whole-machine counter, and this slice's own verification is a large part of the load. Run the full suite, C-052 rehearsal, X-006 and WindowMutants serially, as separate engine runs. Price the pool cost of any test a review finding enlarges.
learned.evidence: Build #1 was killed at +0.54 GB with 3 acting runs overlapping. Build #10 was killed at +0.79 GB. A verify lap measured +0.31 GB: full suite about +0.17, C-052 about +0.11. Review fix F5 raised the rehearsal tree from about 2,000 to 30,150 folders. Validate saw the full suite push paged pool up about 143 MB (FMfn +145K).

learned.lesson: Critique findings were disposed by a model and every one was accepted-pending, none overridden. Each fix added machinery, which fed the harness growth. critique-review did not run (a sizing decision). Next time, put a 'does this decide anything before the fork is settled, and can raw logs plus completeness do it' check in the critic's brief for harness findings.
learned.evidence: Critique attempts 2/4/6/8 disposed 13, 20, 31 and 45 findings, all marked as answered by a model and untriaged in gate precision. The accepted M3, N3, X2, M4, N1, N2, X5 and R2-N1 added the pressure step, settle gate and unfixed arms that design 10 removed.

learned.lesson: The three LastAccess/HeldOpenTree test failures predate the slice and were never triaged. They were reported as 'known' by every one of six validations. Until someone triages them, the full suite is never green and a regression in the last-access area (the SC-070/074 lead in the original brief) is invisible.
learned.evidence: Failing at afd021d: HeldOpenTreeTests.TheScanChangesNoEntrysMetadata, HeldOpenTreeTests.APlainListingOfTheControlFolderMovesItsLastAccessTime and LastAccessTests.AFolderThatRefusesWriteAttributesIsListedPlainlyAndCountedInFull. 'Expected 2026-09-28... Actual 2026-09-30'; fsutil DisableLastAccess=2. Full suite 537 passed, 3 failed at b7e9c18.

missed.what: The critique never asked whether a spelling an unelevated user can open reaches the store unmatched. The design contract itself said 'A loopback SMB root (\\localhost\C$\ProgramData\...) is not matched; that gap is documented.' That contradicts Q-182's assumption that other spellings are caught. m1 only asked for subst, Volume{GUID} and 8.3. A check someone could write: for every spelling the local user can open, including \\localhost\C$ and \\127.0.0.1\C$, feed it through the published exe and assert Refused or skippedStores 1.
missed.caught_by: validate #2 (real contact): the published exe given \\localhost\C$\...\Layers\<id>\Files\Windows\Media returned Completed, read 95 files and 14 folders from inside the store. Fixed in build #7.

missed.what: 'First touch only, capped near 0.33 GB per boot' went unchallenged. Critique M2 used it as a premise, and it was written into user-facing texts (KnownWorkarounds.cs:29, :38, :46: 'read for the first time since the PC was restarted'). It rested on one investigation probe of a repeat walk. Nobody repeated the walk through the app's SizeProbe path. A check: any text or argument that bounds the cost of the precaution-off position must cite a repeat-walk measurement on the app's own probe path.
missed.caught_by: validate #2 (real contact): 4 repeat walks of Globalization each added +5 WCsc and +5 System 0x120089 handles. Text corrected in build #7.

missed.what: Critique attempts 2, 4 and 6 added a verdict engine to a person-run harness before the fork it routed was decided: settle gate, per-pool drift VOID, tolerance row, pressure step with a positive control, unfixed afd021d arms, WCIFS-UNATTRIBUTED, and ScanArm L/S/P arms. Spike #87 decided outcome C, so none of it could ever produce a pass. A check: 'if the harness logged only raw nets and completeness, would the next decision be any different?'
missed.caught_by: design attempt 10 and the narrowing request, after about seven code-review send-backs of the judge (R2-N1, R3-1, R4-1, R4-2, R2-R3-3, R3-2, M1). The judge was deleted and handed to SC-128.

missed.what: Finding F5's fix, 'size the rehearsal tree so a scan lasts at least 10x the poll interval', raised the -Rehearse tree from about 2,000 to 30,150 folders. It was not priced against the engine's 0.5 GB per-run kernel-pool guard, on a slice whose subject is kernel pool. A check: any review fix that enlarges a pool-touching test states its expected pool cost.
missed.caught_by: the engine's kernel-memory guard: build #10 was stopped at +0.79 GB while running the rehearsal and full-suite checks, and build #1 had been stopped at +0.54 GB.

what_went_wrong: DONE (c) was never reachable inside the loop and was only narrowed out at design attempt 10. Before that: 6 spikes (4 ended 'built anyway' with nothing measured), 8 designs and 8 critiques, 11 builds, 13 code reviews and 6 validations. The slice's real finding, spike #87's outcome C, arrived after three designs had assumed outcome A.

About seven code-review send-backs (builds 3-5 and 7-9) went on PoolWatch's verdict judge and harness text. That judge was deleted or handed to SC-128 when design 10 narrowed the slice. Builds 8-9 changed only src comments.

The picked-root refusal was built unconditional (critique F1) and Q-186 then answered off-lifts-both. Reversing it cost validate #2/#3, builds #7-#9 and code-review #10-#11, across code, user-facing text, tests and AA-015.

Twelve code-review laps passed code with two defects that only validate found on the published exe and real store: the \\localhost\C$ root reaching the store unmatched, and the 'first time only' leak text.
The engine's kernel-memory guard killed build #1 (+0.54 GB, with 3 acting runs overlapping) and build #10 (+0.79 GB). The slice's verification is itself pool-heavy.

Spike #87's per-mark evidence for the outcome-C decision that narrowed the slice was left under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and was partly lost. Only L.json, skips.log and a folder count were recovered into docs/design/SL-095-runs/. marks.jsonl and events.log are gone, which the record states as a gap in the risk-spike stage.
Design 10 assumed all scanner code was new because acf169eb was 'not on slice/SL-095'. It did not check, even though builds #2-#6 had produced reviewed scanner code.
The three last-access test failures were repeated in all six validations and never triaged, so the full suite never went green.
unknowns: Does wcifs leak again on repeat walks of already-touched layer entries (validate: +5 per walk, n=4, one subtree, probably through SizeProbe), or only on first touch (investigation: second walk 0)? The answer decides whether the precaution-off text 'later scans can add more' is right, and whether a scan-after-scan mechanism exists at all.

What produces the reported ~21 GB paged and ~10 GB nonpaged? A cold exe-full scan with the store excluded is predicted at 3-4.4 GiB. Does it stay under the 6 GiB per-arm guard? Is the FMfn/File/NtfF retention reclaimable cache? One data point: deleting the rehearsal's 30,150-folder tree dropped FMfn live by 118,863 and paged pool by 92 MB without a Restart. This is SC-128's.

Does a C: scan with the precaution on reach a second live WCI store when Windows Sandbox or a Docker windowsfilter layer is running? Spike #87 covered one boot with only the CmService zygote, and no Sandbox exists on this PC.
Are the three red last-access tests environmental (DisableLastAccess=2, set timestamps not sticking), or does a scan really change last-access metadata?
Does the 8.3 branch of the root-spelling test actually assert on this volume? The test asserts only when a distinct short name exists, and nobody inspected which branch ran.

candidates.title: Triage the three red last-access tests (LastAccessTests.AFolderThatRefusesWriteAttributes..., HeldOpenTreeTests.TheScanChangesNoEntrysMetadata, HeldOpenTreeTests.APlainListingOfTheControlFolderMovesItsLastAccessTime): environment fault or real scan side effect
candidates.why: They failed at afd021d and through all six SL-095 validations, always reported as 'pre-existing' and never diagnosed. DisableLastAccess=2 on this PC, and one test is named TheScanChangesNoEntrysMetadata, which touches the SC-070/074 lead from the original brief. Until they are triaged the full suite is never green and a regression in that area would hide in the noise.

candidates.title: Measure whether a C: scan with the precaution on reaches a second live WCI store while Windows Sandbox or Docker windowsfilter is running
candidates.why: O-085 limited ContainerLayerStore to the single Layers path on spike #87's evidence, from one fresh boot with only the CmService zygote running. The design's third decidable disagreement was flagged would_force_resynthesis. The reopen condition is a raw WC* rise in an exe-full arm that reports notScanned >= 1 and opensUnderExcludedStore = 0, and no such run exists. It needs a person to start Sandbox. It is separate from SC-128's pool-growth work.

candidates.title: Close or notice the documented root-spelling gaps in ContainerLayerStore: a net use drive mapped to \\localhost\C$, a hosts/DNS alias of this PC, and an admin-created share over ProgramData
candidates.why: Q-182 assumed every spelling of a picked root is caught. Validate found \\localhost\C$ reached the store, and it was fixed. These three remain, documented as not covered. The net use case was tested only through symlinks to the share, because creating a mapping changes network settings. When GetFinalPathNameByHandleW fails, the string verdict stands silently. A notice or a refusal in that case would keep the Q-182 promise honest.
